newsitem.title: LATVIA: C.BANK CHIEF INSISTS ON BALANCED BUDGET.
newsitem.headline: C.BANK CHIEF INSISTS ON BALANCED BUDGET.

text.p: Latvian central bank chief Einar Repshe on Wednesday insisted that the country needed to keep to a balanced budget or risk hurting economic development.
"Moving from a balanced budget would be a big blow to Latvia's economy," Repshe told a news conference.
The finance ministry has warned that tax collection is below the planned level and that there is a risk of a budget deficit of 10 million lats to 12 million lats.
The new government of Guntar Krasts also wants to have a balanced budget this year. It has pledged definitely to have one next year if it turns out to impossible for 1997.
Repshe said the biggest achievement of outgoing prime minister Andris Shkele was the passing of the balanced budget.

He warned that if the state moved into deficit again then interest rates would rise and banks would again make easy profits from T-bills rather than trying to make money from lending and helping economic growth by extending credits.
